fatal_errors: The proposed Al addition to an unspecified BCC refractory HEA does not reconstruct the target intervention of Zr alloying in as-cast FCC/B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
No cited evidence supports the claimed improvement in corrosion resistance from Al addition.
The material composition is not specified, so the proposed Al range, phase evolution, and property trends cannot be interpreted reproducibly across the diverse RHEA family.
The hypothesis omits the target's composition-dependent tradeoff: moderate Zr maximizes mechanical and creep properties, whereas higher Zr gives the best corrosion resistance.
explanation: The response addresses the general application and proposes a single alloying intervention with a dose-series experiment, so it has some problem alignment. However, it is scientifically distinct from the hidden result in starting alloy, crystal structure, alloying element, phases, test conditions, and composition-dependent outcomes. Its strengthening mechanism is generically plausible, and E1–E2 provide limited support for Al-induced strengthening and nanoscale creep trends, but E2 concerns different alloy systems and E3 does not support Al addition. None of the evidence establishes corrosion improvement, and no passivation mechanism is proposed. The baseline and boundaries are too broad to make quantitative predictions. The experiment includes controls and relevant measurements, but lacks a defined RHEA composition, corrosion medium, creep protocol, durability metric, effect-size threshold, and statistical criterion; therefore its falsification rule is only moderately discriminating.
